# Signed inverse arms for a general concave profile

This note extends the record formulas beyond a source at the profile maximum. The finite-knot replacement extension is stated with its exact dependency; independent audits are requested. No sharp cap inequality or mixed-integer conclusion is claimed.

Let d=m+1>=2. Let r be a continuous nonnegative concave profile on a compact axial interval containing zero in its interior, with r(0)>0 and maximum R>0. Continuity at the axial endpoints is included, as for the closed convex-body profiles used here; a bare concave function with an artificial downward endpoint jump is excluded. The planar component measure has density r(z)^(m-1)/2 on |x|<=r(z). At endpoint heights zero the measure is defined by its interior density; those boundary points have zero planar mass. Write V for total mass.

For 0<=v<=R, let the closed superlevel interval be

    {z:r(z)>=v}=[-B(v),A(v)].

The arms A,B are finite continuous concave nonincreasing functions, and A(0),B(0)>0. They may be negative above r(0). Their sum is nonnegative everywhere. These facts follow from convexity and nesting of the superlevel hypograph. A positive interval of maximizers is allowed. Initial/final flat portions of the arms represent vertical endpoint faces or top plateaus.

For s>0 put

    P(s)=int 1_{z+s x>=0} f(x,z)dx dz,
    C(s)=int delta(z+s x) f(x,z)dx dz,
    M(s)=int z delta(z+s x) f(x,z)dx dz.

Coarea is normalized by the raw normal length, as in the existing profile notes.

## 1. Direct layer decomposition, without a projective change

For any integrable test g, layer cake in the factor r(z)^(m-1) gives

    int g f
      =1/2 int_0^R v^(m-1) int_(-B(v))^(A(v))
                         [g(v,z)+g(-v,z)] dz dv
       +(m-1)/2 int_0^R v^(m-2) int_(-v)^v
                         int_(-B(v))^(A(v)) g(x,z) dz dx dv.       (1)

For m=1 the second term is absent, so no negative power at v=0 is used. To prove (1), for each fixed x use

    r^(m-1)1_{|x|<=r}
      =|x|^(m-1)1_{|x|<=r}
       +int_(|x|)^R (m-1)v^(m-2)1_{v<=r}dv

and apply Fubini, or Tonelli first to nonnegative g. In particular

    V=m int_0^R v^(m-1)[A(v)+B(v)]dv.                         (2)

## 2. Exact piecewise record kernels

For t real define the even function

    j_s(t,v)=m v^(m-1)|t|/2,                       |t|>=s v;
      s(m+1)v^m/4+(m-1)v^(m-2)t^2/(4s),           |t|<=s v.   (3)

At m=1 the quadratic term is absent. The two expressions agree at their boundary. Then

    P(s)=V/2+int_0^R[j_s(A(v),v)-j_s(B(v),v)]dv.              (4)

Indeed (1) applied to the cap indicator first gives P=int[G_s(A,v)-G_s(-B,v)], where

    G_s(t,v)=v^(m-1)[(t+s v)_++(t-s v)_+]/2
          +(m-1)v^(m-2)int_(-v)^v(t+s x)_+ dx/2.

The identity G_s(t,v)-G_s(-t,v)=m v^(m-1)t follows from q_+-(-q)_+=q and symmetry in x. Expanding the positive-part integral shows G_s(t,v)=j_s(t,v)+m v^(m-1)t/2, which proves (3)-(4).

Away from t=+-s v define

    c_s(t,v)=m v^(m-1) sign(t)/2,                 |t|>s v;
      (m-1)v^(m-2)t/(2s),                        |t|<s v;    (5)

    k_s(t,v)=0,                                  |t|>s v;
      -s(m+1)v^m/4+(m-1)v^(m-2)t^2/(4s),         |t|<s v.    (6)

Then

    C(s)=int_0^R[c_s(A(v),v)+c_s(B(v),v)]dv,
    M(s)=int_0^R[k_s(A(v),v)-k_s(B(v),v)]dv.                  (7)

For justification, each A(v)-s v is strictly decreasing from a positive value. Each A(v)+s v is concave, starts positive, and can cross zero at most once. If a concave function starting positive had two distinct zero points, its chord slope to the first would be negative while the slope between the two would be zero, contradicting decreasing chord slopes. Thus the exceptional equalities in (5)-(6) occur at at most two levels per arm, and have zero dv measure.

Moving the cap threshold from zero to epsilon replaces the arms in (4) by A-epsilon and B+epsilon and preserves (2). Differentiation under the integral is justified by the bounded piecewise derivatives on any compact positive-slope neighborhood. It gives (5) and the coarea formula. Differentiating (4) in s similarly gives k_s=-s partial_s j_s. Direct coarea differentiation of the cap integral gives P'(s)=int x delta(z+s x)f, so M(s)=-sP'(s), proving (6)-(7). Every cutting line passes through the body's interior; no supporting-line boundary mass is introduced.

For nonnegative arms, the new integrated j differs from the earlier J by the common constant sR^(m+1)/4; the new integrated k differs from earlier K by its negative. Both constants cancel between arms, agreeing with the previous formulas.

## 3. Zero slope and finite branch partitions

At s=0 use the separate formulas

    P(0)=V/2+(m/2)int_0^R v^(m-1)(|A(v)|-|B(v)|)dv,
    C(0)=r(0)^m,
    M(0)=0.                                                   (8)

The first follows directly by measuring the positive-z part of each superlevel interval. The second is the actual section at z=0. The first zero of either arm gives r(0), unless both remain nonnegative to R, in which case r(0)=R.

For a fixed finite collection of positive slopes, partition each arm at its internal roots of A=+s v and A=-s v, and at its internal zero if present. There are at most two roots per positive slope and at most one additional zero. Concavity and the unchanged interpolation values retain every branch interval after replacement. At the top R the required uncrossed-branch inequalities persist if the completed arm value rises. If a negative crossing already occurred internally, concavity from the positive initial value prevents any return to zero and retains the negative branch up to R.

On each branch cell, V and each kernel (3),(5),(6) depend only on the three integrals

    int v^(m-2)A,   int v^(m-1)A,   int v^(m-2)A^2,

plus integrals of fixed powers of v. For m=1 it suffices to preserve int A and the fixed cell endpoints; artificial weight w=1 can preserve extra moments harmlessly. The zero-slope formula is likewise retained by the zero-root partition and the first-degree moment.

## 4. Applying the exact replacement theorem to signed arms

The local proof in candidate a260044e1f85011a does not require a nonnegative arm for its compact curvature representation, strict convexity, moment dual, contact lemma, or min/max interpolation. On an internal cell, keeping both endpoint values gives a common lower bound equal to their minimum. On a terminal cell, the completed endpoint is at least the original endpoint, so the same common lower bound holds. These bounds replace the previously used nonnegativity in the dominated-convergence argument. Nonincrease and concavity are unchanged. Therefore its internal eight-atom and terminal seven-atom replacements apply to signed arms as well.

Assemble them with the same join slope inequalities, preserving every internal branch crossing. Each completed terminal arm value can only increase. The sum of the two new arms is concave, is positive at level zero, and is nonnegative at level R because its original value there was nonnegative. It is consequently nonnegative at every intermediate level.

Thus the set

    {(z,v):0<=v<=R, -Bhat(v)<=z<=Ahat(v)}

is an actual nonempty convex hypograph with nested level intervals. It reconstructs a concave piecewise-affine physical profile. The original axial endpoints remain fixed. The source remains interior, and its height is preserved by the zero-level crossings or the retained top inequalities. There is no projective transformation of the physical measure.

All records (2),(4),(7),(8) at the fixed finite list of slopes are preserved exactly. With q positive slopes there are at most 2q+2 cells per arm, so a conservative bound is 9(2q+2) curvature locations per arm, including join points. The count is not claimed sharp.

The conclusion is an exact finite-knot reduction for these records for every concave homothetic profile with an interior source. It is not a proof that the corrected scalar intervals intersect, and it supplies no transfer to arbitrary mixed-integer fibers.

# Signed inverse arms for a general concave profile

**Signed inverse arms remove the horizontal-maximum restriction**

For any continuous nonnegative concave physical profile with an interior source, its superlevel interval is [-B(v),A(v)] with concave nonincreasing signed arms. Exact piecewise kernels give all cap, coarea, and section-moment records. Applying local replacement on thresholds A=+/-sv and A=0 preserves any finite menu and reconstructs an actual concave profile, even when the source is below the maximum.

Scope limits: Continuity/closed hypograph is an explicit corrected hypothesis. No projective density change is made. The general-profile two-mixture inequality is not proved.
